correctness.rationale: The claim has matching upper and lower bounds.  The upper bound follows from Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:2609.00569v1 using the explicit acyclic part orientation C to B to A, whose maximum reachable set has size six.  The lower bound uses one fully specified preference profile on five colors; exhaustive exact enumeration checks all 5^8 color maps, all 2940 proper maps, and a blocking cycle in every proper case.  Rankings can be extended arbitrarily beyond five because only five-colorings are excluded.

evidence: The paper says its exact elementary families are paths, cycles, and complete bipartite graphs.
Appendix A gives a triangular-prism profile with no stable four-coloring, hence only a five-color lower bound transferable by monotonicity.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general reachability theorem supplies the six-color upper bound here, but no published lower theorem in the inspected source forces six.  The prism result is strictly weaker under implication.

value.rationale: The complete tripartite family is a natural next test after the initiating paper’s complete-bipartite exact theorem.  K_{2,3,3} is the first complete-tripartite part-size profile by order whose elementary part-order reachability upper bound can be six, and the certificate shows the new level is attained.  This is a motivated exact invariant, not a parameter renaming or a recomputation of a known table.
